bull.b: Cloudflare is sustaining rapid top-line expansion across its subscription and usage-based platform. Continued growth at this scale indicates broadening customer adoption and supports greater operating leverage, reinvestment in the network, and durable competitive positioning over the next several quarters.

High net retention shows existing customers are expanding their Cloudflare usage through additional products, higher tiers, or greater consumption. Growth in large accounts further strengthens revenue durability, enterprise penetration, and the land-and-expand economics of the platform.

Positive and improving free cash flow demonstrates that Cloudflare is converting strong demand into internally generated funding despite negative GAAP earnings. Its substantial cash and securities balance provides resources for network investment, product development, and strategic flexibility.

bear.b: Leverage is high relative to the company’s software profile and reduces financial flexibility if growth slows or funding conditions tighten. Debt service and refinancing needs can compete with investment priorities, while the reported cash-flow coverage ratio remains modest.

Persistent GAAP losses show that revenue scale has not yet translated into durable bottom-line profitability. A widening TTM operating loss despite higher sales raises execution concerns and leaves the business more dependent on continued growth and non-GAAP adjustments.

Lower gross margin and elevated planned network investment could constrain operating leverage as Cloudflare scales traffic and expands infrastructure. If network costs remain elevated, stronger revenue growth may translate less efficiently into durable earnings and cash generation.
